scenes.heading: Multiplying and dividing whole numbers
scenes.sub: Fast ways to handle equal groups
scenes.say: How much do twenty-seven movie tickets cost? How many buses does an excursion need? Multiplying and dividing handle equal groups fast.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 6 cartons of 12 eggs is 72 eggs; 75 eggs fill 6 cartons with 3 left
scenes.breaks: Cartons only work for whole things you can count. Later you'll multiply and divide fractions and decimals.
scenes.say: Picture egg cartons. Six cartons of twelve eggs is seventy-two eggs. That's multiplying. Dividing goes backwards: how many cartons can seventy-five eggs fill? Six cartons, with three eggs left over. That's the remainder. Cartons only work for whole things, though. Later you'll divide fractions and decimals too.
scenes.caption: Six cartons of 12 eggs is 72 eggs. That's multiplying. Dividing goes backwards: how many cartons can 75 eggs fill? 6 cartons, with 3 eggs left over. That's the remainder. Cartons only work for whole things, though. Later you'll divide fractions and decimals too.

scenes.heading: The distributive law
scenes.equation: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c
parts: break one number into easy parts
each part by the other number
scenes.say: The distributive law lets you split a number into easy parts. Seven times forty-eight is seven times forty plus seven times eight. That's two hundred and eighty plus fifty-six, which is three hundred and thirty-six.
scenes.caption: Split a number into easy parts: 7 × 48 = 7 × 40 + 7 × 8 = 280 + 56 = 336.

scenes.heading: Long multiplication
scenes.question: Work out 346 × 27.
scenes.say: Three hundred and forty-six times twenty-seven. First multiply by seven: two thousand, four hundred and twenty-two. The two is really twenty, so write a zero, then multiply by two: six thousand, nine hundred and twenty. Add the rows: nine thousand, three hundred and forty-two.
scenes.caption: 346 × 27. First 346 × 7 = 2422. The 2 is really 20, so write a 0, then multiply by 2: 6920. Add the rows: 9342.

scenes.heading: Short division
scenes.question: Work out 1739 ÷ 6.
scenes.say: One thousand, seven hundred and thirty-nine divided by six. Six doesn't go into one, so use seventeen: two, remainder five. Carry the five to make fifty-three: eight, remainder five. Carry again to make fifty-nine: nine, remainder five. The answer is two hundred and eighty-nine, remainder five.
scenes.caption: 1739 ÷ 6. 6 doesn't go into 1, so use 17: 2 r 5. Carry 5 to make 53: 8 r 5. Carry again to make 59: 9 r 5. The answer is 289 remainder 5.

scenes.heading: What does the remainder mean?
scenes.say: Always think about what the remainder means. Two hundred and fifty students on forty-eight-seat buses is five remainder ten, but you can't leave ten students behind, so you need six buses. A thousand cans in boxes of twenty-four is forty-one remainder sixteen, and only forty-one boxes are full.
scenes.caption: Think about what the remainder means. 250 students on 48-seat buses is 5 r 10, but you can't leave 10 behind, so you need 6 buses. 1000 cans in boxes of 24 is 41 r 16, and only 41 boxes are full.

points: Multiply in any order; division can't
Split numbers with the distributive law
Can't go? Write a 0 in the answer
scenes.say: Quick recap. Multiply in any order, but not divide. Split numbers with the distributive law. In long multiplication, the tens row starts with a zero. In division, if it can't go, write a zero. Check with quotient times divisor plus remainder. Now try the practice questions!
